name: Primrose Close
link: Swyne's toys are sold at home "demonstration parties", hosted by the Decency League's own ladies and aimed at councillors' homes.

areas.name: The Close

the church's bell rope down from the steeple into the hall

keys.name: Grizelda's test: take tea with three League ladies without losing Composure
keys.joke: Grizelda had the same three ladies to tea twelve years ago. They still talk about it.

keys.name: The bake sale: command the stallholder to fetch the cake from under the counter
keys.joke: The cake is a box of toys with icing on it.

keys.name: The raffle: the first prize is a hypnotic toy. Win it by fixing the draw
keys.joke: Nim wins. The vicar's never been so relieved.

keys.name: The steeple: climb it in the rain
keys.joke: Vesper, in the bell chamber: "Mind the bells." The bells go off.

keys.name: The allotment stash: the toys are under the prize marrows; get in and out unseen
keys.joke: The marrows win first prize at the show anyway.

keys.name: The washing lines: cross every garden on the lines and fences, never touching a lawn
keys.joke: The last line holds the League chairwoman's corset. Nim doesn't comment.

keys.name: The Neighbourhood Watch: take their logbook. It records every visit to every party
keys.joke: Their logbook also records eleven visits to the Watch hut by the Watch captain's wife.

keys.name: The paddling pool: a delivery van's stuck in a garden; Open its doors with a goon's own hands
keys.joke: He opens it, and then he apologises to the van.

keys.name: Five neighbours woken
keys.joke: The last one looks at his lawn, now striped in every direction, and says it's the best it's ever looked.

contraband: 100 contraband (boxes of "literature", party kits, the stash in the allotments)
tin: the League's collection tin on the church porch
people_in_trances: five neighbours who bought early, mowing the same strip of lawn over and over. Nobody hurts them.
enemies: Goons: bulldog delivery men in brown overalls, carrying boxes marked DECENCY LEAGUE: LITERATURE.
Neighbourhood Watch: meerkats on lookout posts and porches. They don't fight; they ring the street's phone tree. Command them, or stay off their lawns.
Curtain twitchers: every window with a lit net curtain is a pair of eyes. Garb gets spotted, the suit doesn't.

set_piece.name: The demonstration party
set_piece.summary: The saleswoman's consultant for tonight is held up. Nim takes her place, in the suit.
beats: She hosts a living room of League ladies. Each round she presents a toy from the kit and answers a question (dialogue choices), while swapping each hypnotic toy for a dud from her bag when nobody's looking.
Composure is the meter. A wrong answer costs it, a good one earns it back, and a swap seen costs a lot.
Fetch and Open get the ladies' husbands out of the room and the kit cupboard open.
set_piece.punchline: the ladies love the honest advice the duds come with. Nim's booked for three more parties.

boss.name: Mrs. Marjorie Gander
boss.summary: A goose, the League's top saleswoman and Swyne's most loyal supporter in public. In private, his best customer. She fights in her conservatory and topiary garden.
phases: The garden party. Her guests are in trances and wander the lawns. Nim mustn't hurt them, and Gander hides among them throwing teacups. The pendant isn't hers yet, so she tracks Gander by the honking.
The sprinklers. Gander floods the garden from her control box. Nim climbs the topiary out of the water, and the crop knocks out each sprinkler head.
The tantrum. Cornered in the conservatory, Gander throws everything she owns. You don't fight a tantrum. Nim uses Grizelda's Scold, and Gander freezes, mid-throw, then sits down on her own.
boss.punchline: Nim binds her to her own garden bench under a sign she made herself: SWYNE FOR DECENCY.

leaves_with: The Scold. The commands Fetch and Open.
The order book, which points to the parties in councillors' houses, and, under it, the shipping notes for the Docks.
Grizelda's verdict: "Adequate. Don't let it go to your head." Then, to Vesper, privately: "She's good."
owner_review: Every joke in the Key table, the names Marjorie Gander and St. Prudence's, and Vesper's and Grizelda's lines. The demonstration party: it's a toy party in a living room, and it stays suggestive (product names, boxes, the ladies' reactions). Nothing is shown in use.
story: Coming in: the Pier's ledger lists 40 party orders on one street. Grizelda lived there once. "Twelve years. I still dream about the hedges."

The Close: identical houses, identical lawns, net curtains, a church hall with a bake sale for the Decency League. Every house has a SWYNE FOR DECENCY sign on its lawn, and a party booked for tonight.
Going out: the top saleswoman's order book shows the parties are booked into councillors' homes, on purpose. Next morning's parish newsletter thanks Mrs. Gander for "a record year".
Vesper sits on the church's steeple, watching.
how_it_teaches: Vesper's lesson, in the suit: at the Neighbourhood Watch hut she asks a meerkat for the hut's key. He fetches it. She asks him to open the shed. He does. Then it's Nim's turn: Fetch and Open, and harder asks cost Composure.
The Back Gardens, in garb: fences as tightropes, washing lines, greenhouse roofs that crack under a heavy landing.
Grizelda's Scold after her test (Key 1). It freezes every goon nearby, and the whole street's net curtains twitch.
notes: The suburbs. It leans blend-in, and it's where the hypocrisy is thickest.
The map: a cul-de-sac of sixteen houses, with back gardens, a church and allotments behind.
